quiz.question: What is machine code?

answers.answer: English-like commands the CPU reads directly
Raw binary instructions (1s and 0s) that the CPU understands
A type of programming language similar to Python
A file format used to store source code

quiz.explanation: Machine code is the raw binary (1s and 0s) that a CPU actually executes. Every program eventually becomes machine code before it runs.

quiz.question: Why do humans almost never write machine code directly?

answers.answer: It runs too slowly on modern CPUs
It is illegal to distribute machine code
It is too error-prone and nearly impossible to read at scale

quiz.explanation: Writing raw binary is extremely tedious and error-prone, which is why higher-level tools like assembly and programming languages exist.

quiz.question: What does a single machine code instruction typically do?

answers.answer: Runs an entire application at once
One tiny operation, like adding numbers or moving data
Compiles source code into an executable

quiz.explanation: Each machine code instruction performs just one very small operation. Programs are built from millions of these tiny steps running in sequence.
